MATCHING & SORTING · 31 WORKSHEETS · AGE 2

Matching and sorting worksheets for 2-year-olds — printables.

Thirty-one matching and sorting worksheets from the owner’s own bold, friendly artwork: same-and-different pairs, animal twins and shadows, baby animals, big and small, color and shape sorts — every one a whole activity on a single page. Download and print buttons sit right under every picture.

SOLVE THEM ON SCREEN TOO

Every sheet has an on-screen twin.

Each of these thirty-one sheets can be solved right here on the website in Class 10 — Matching and Sorting (Age 2): the drawing layer sits on the picture, little hands draw the matching lines with a finger, a stylus or the mouse, and every child’s drawing is saved for next time. Open the class and start with Match Same Colors.

WORKSHEET · MATCHING & SORTING · AGE 2

Match Same Colors Worksheet

A printable match-same-colors worksheet for 2-year-olds: a blue balloon, a yellow duck, a red apple and a green leaf each find their same-color twin on the other side — on paper or on screen.

Teaching tips
HOW TO USE IT

Three little steps.

  1. 1

    Say the color

    Point at the balloon and say “blue!”. Then the duck — “yellow!”. Do all four.

  2. 2

    Find the twin

    Look on the other side: which one is the same color as the balloon?

  3. 3

    Draw the line

    Draw a line from each thing to its same-color friend — four proud lines.

WORKSHEET · MATCHING & SORTING · AGE 2

Match Same Animals Worksheet

A printable match-same-animals worksheet for toddlers: a puppy, a kitten and a bunny each have a look-alike on the other side — draw the line that joins the twins, on paper or on screen.

Teaching tips
HOW TO USE IT

Three little steps.

  1. 1

    Name them

    A dog, a cat, a rabbit — say hello to each one.

  2. 2

    Spot the twin

    Find the same animal on the other side of the page.

  3. 3

    Join them

    Draw a line from each animal to its twin — three lines, three matches.

Find the Matching Pair Worksheet

HOW TO USE IT

Three little steps.

    Pick one

    Choose any picture — the apple, for example.

  2. 2

    Hunt its twin

  3. 3

    Circle the pair

    Circle both, then pick a new picture and hunt again.
